articles.text: LǏ PÍNG: Ēi! Tāngmǔ, nǐ hǎo a!
LǏ PÍNG: Hey! Hi, Tom!
TĀNGMǓ: Nǐ hǎo, Lǐ Píng! Lái kàn shū ma?
TOM: Hi, Lǐ Píng. Did you come here to do some reading?
LǏ PÍNG: Chīle wǎnfàn, chūlai zǒuzou, dào túshūguǎn kànkan xīn dàode zázhì.
LǏ PÍNG: After dinner I went out for a walk and came to the library to read through some of the new magazines.
TĀNGMǓ: Nǐ zuì xǐhuande Yīngwén zázhì shi shénme?
TOM: What's your favorite English magazine?
LǏ PÍNG: Ng, Xīnwén Zhōukān.
LǏ PÍNG: Um, Newsweek.
TĀNGMǓ: Wèishénme ne?
TOM: Why?
LǏ PÍNG: Xīnwén Zhōukān hěn hǎo, duì xué Yīngwén hěn yǒu bāngzhu.
LǏ PÍNG: Newsweek is very good. It's a big help in learning English.
TĀNGMǓ: Duì, kàn zhèige zázhì, yìfāngmiàn kěyi xué Yīngwén, yìfāngmiàn kěyi zhīdao Měiguo shèhuìde qíngkuàng, shi bú cuò. Zhèige xīngqī yǒu shénme yǒu yìside wénzhāng ma?
TOM: Right. When you read it, you can study English at the same time you learn about conditions in American society; it is good. Are there any interesting articles in it this week?
LǏ PÍNG: Yǒu, yǒu yìpiān guānyú nánnǚ píngděngde wénzhāng hěn yǒu yìsi.
LǏ PÍNG: Yes, there's an article about equality of the sexes that's very interesting.
TĀNGMǓ: Ou, "nánnǚ píngděng"... wǒde nǚpéngyou duì zhèige tímù hěn yǒu yánjiū. Zěnme? Nǐ yě duì zhèige wèntí yǒu xìngqù ma?
TOM: Oh, "equality of the sexes"... My girlfriend is an expert on the subject. Don't tell me — are you interested in that issue too?
LǏ PÍNG: Yǒu, wǒ yǒu xìngqù, érqiě xiǎng zhīdao nǐmende kànfǎ. Wǒ kěyi wèn jǐge wèntí ma?
LǏ PÍNG: Yes, I am, and I'd also like to know your views on it. Can I ask a few questions?
TĀNGMǓ: Dāngrán, qǐng wèn ba!
TOM: Sure. What would you like to know?
LǏ PÍNG: Zhèipiān wénzhāng shuō, zài hěn duō dìfang yuè lái yuè liúxíng nánnǚ tóngjū le. Ē, duìbuqǐ...
LǏ PÍNG: The article says that in a lot of places cohabitation is getting more and more common. Uh, excuse me...
TĀNGMǓ: Méi shenme, nǐ shuōxiaqu.
TOM: Not at all, go on.

LǏ PÍNG: Zhèipiān wénzhāng hái shuō zhèizhǒng shì hé fùnǚde dìwèi yǒu guānxi. Zhèi yìdiǎn wǒ zhēnshi bù dǒng le. Zhōngguo rénde chuántǒng guānniàn shi, fùnǚ méiyou jiéhūn, bù yīnggāi hé tāde nánpéngyou zhù zài yìqǐ.

LǏ PÍNG: It also said in the article that this is related to the status of women. I really don't understand that point. The traditional Chinese idea is that a woman should not live with her boyfriend before they get married.

TĀNGMǓ: Wǒmende guānniàn bú tài yíyàng. Yìxiē fùnǚ, tèbié shi zhīshi fùnǚ, tāmen bú yào kào xiānsheng shēnghuó, tāmen yào yǒu dúlìde jīngjì hé shèhuì dìwèi. Xiàng wǒde nǚpéngyou, tā jiù yǒu zhèiyàngde kànfǎ. Érqiě wǒ xiǎng, tóngjūde wèntí hé hěn duō shìqing yǒu guānxi, bù zhǐ shi fùnǚde dìwèi wèntí.

TOM: We have a somewhat different concept. Some women, especially women intellectuals, don't want to depend on their husbands in order to live; they want to have independent economic and social status. Like my girlfriend — that's the way her view is. But also, I think that living together has to do with a lot of things. It's not just a question of the status of women.
LǏ PÍNG: Rúguǒ kěyi tánde huà, nǐ gěi wo jiǎngjiang zěnmeyàng?
LǏ PÍNG: If it's all right to talk about it, would you tell me more?
TĀNGMǓ: Hǎo, zhèiyàngr ba, wǒ gēn ni tántan wǒde shì, nǐ jiù zhīdao wǒmen zěnme xiǎng le. Wǒde nǚpéngyou, tā shi xué yīde. Xué yī bú shi yíjiàn róngyide shìr. Tā hái yào zài dàxué xuéxí liùnián.

TOM: Okay, how about this. I'll tell you about my situation, and then you'll know the way we think. My girlfriend is studying medicine. Studying medicine isn't the easiest thing. She still has six more years of university.
LǏ PÍNG: Nà nǐmen shénme shíhou jiéhūn ne?
LǏ PÍNG: Then when are you getting married?
TĀNGMǓ: Xiànzài wǒmen hái bù xiǎng jiéhūn.
TOM: We don't want to get married just yet.
LǏ PÍNG: Wèishénme? Nǐmen juéde jiéle hūn, yǒule háizi huì hěn máfan, shi bu shi?
LǏ PÍNG: Why not? You think that once you get married and have children it'll be a lot of trouble, right?

TĀNGMǓ: Bú shi zhèige yìsi. Jiùshi wǒmen jiéhūnle, yě bù yídìng mǎshang yào háizi. Zhòngyàode shi wǒmen zhèi yíbèizi yào zuò shénme, hái méiyou hǎohāor xiǎngguo ne. Yīnggāi xiān xiǎng nèige wèntí. Érqiě wǒmen dōu yuànyi zài jiéhūn yǐqián qīngchude zhīdao zìjǐ xǐhuande nèige rén shi yíge shénmeyàngrde rén. Zhèi yě xūyào shíjiān.

TOM: That's not the point. Even if we get married, we won't necessarily have children right away. The important thing is that we haven't even thought out well what we want to do in our lives. We should think about that problem first. What's more, we each want to have a clear idea of what kind of person the other is before we get married. And that takes time.
LǏ PÍNG: Kěshi yǒu rén huì juéde nǐmen zhèiyàng zuò shi yīnwei nǐmen juéde tóngjū bǐ jiéhūn zìyóu.
LǏ PÍNG: But some people will think you are doing this because you feel that living together is freer than marriage.
TĀNGMǓ: Yǒu rén zhème shuō, kěshi wǒ xiǎng tāmen méi dǒng wǒmende zìyóu shi shénme.
TOM: Some people say that, but I don't think they have understood what our freedom is.
LǏ PÍNG: Shi shénme ne?
LǏ PÍNG: What is it, then?
TĀNGMǓ: Měiguo rén juéde zìjǐ kěyi jìhua zìjǐde shēnghuó shi zuì zhòngyàode zìyóu. Rúguǒ Měiguo méiyou zhèizhǒng zìyóu, jiù bú huì yǒu nàme duō rén xiǎng lái Měiguo le. Nǐ shuō wǒ shuōde duì bu duì?

TOM: Americans feel that to be able to plan their own life is the most important freedom. If America didn't have that kind of freedom, there wouldn't be so many people who want to come here. Don't you think I'm right?
LǏ PÍNG: Nǐ shuōde yǒu diǎnr dàolǐ. Ou... wǒ hái wàngle wèn ni: jīnnián xiàtian, nǐde nǚpéngyou néng péi ni dào Xiānggǎng qù ma?
LǏ PÍNG: There's something to what you say. Oh... I forgot to ask you something else: will your girlfriend be able to come with you to Hong Kong this summer?
TĀNGMǓ: Bù xíng. Tā jìhua dào Déguo qù niàn shū. Shǔjiàde shíhou tā yào zài Déguo zhù sānge yuè, nà duì tāde Déwén yídìng hěn yǒu bāngzhu.
TOM: No. She's planning to go to school in Germany. During summer vacation she's going to live in Germany for three months. I'm sure that will help her German a lot.
LǏ PÍNG: Duì.
LǏ PÍNG: That's right.
TĀNGMǓ: Zěnmeyàng, nǐ duì Xīnwén Zhōukān zhèipiān wénzhāng hái yǒu shénme biéde kànfǎ ma?
TOM: So what about it, do you have any other opinions about that article in Newsweek?
LǏ PÍNG: Kànfǎ yǒu. Zhèige tímù hěn dà, wǒmen yǐhòu mànman zài tán.
LǏ PÍNG: Yes, I have other opinions about it. But it's a big topic. We can talk all about it later.
TĀNGMǓ: Hǎo, yǐhòu zài tán.
TOM: Okay, we'll talk about it later.
